headline: NOVA NICKEL BOWS OUT WITH A PRODUCTION BEAT — 21,340t at 7% Above Guidance, Global Lithium Sale Weeks Away
snippet: IGO Limited concluded mining and processing at its Nova Nickel operation in Western Australia on November 9, with final output of 21,340 tonnes of nickel — 7% above the top of revised guidance — capping a 10-year operation that produced 224,277 total tonnes from 2017 to closure. The sale to Global Lithium Resources is expected to complete within weeks, with Global Lithium planning to repurpose Nova's processing plant and infrastructure for its Manna lithium project, completing one of Western Australia's most significant mine-to-battery-metals conversions.

headline: BRAZIL APPROVES 27-MINERAL PRIORITY LIST — Rare Earths, Lithium, Uranium in Tier 1; R$1B BNDES Fund to Follow
snippet: Brazil's National Council for Critical and Strategic Minerals (CIMCE) approved a three-tier priority list of 27 minerals on November 5, with Tier 1 — which unlocks government investment support — including rare earths, lithium, cobalt, nickel, copper, uranium and graphite. The Ministry of Development has until November 20 to submit formal priority supply chain proposals, and a R$1 billion BNDES critical minerals fund is set to follow — positioning Brazil, holder of the world's second-largest rare earth reserves after China, to attract Western mining capital at the moment demand for non-Chinese supply is structurally strongest.

headline: ABRASILVER DRILLS 75m AT 2.44 g/t GOLD + 106 g/t SILVER AT OCULTO — 253m Wide East Zone Halo Confirms Deposit Scale
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp (TSX: ABRA) reported drill results from the Oculto deposit in Argentina with the headline hole returning 75 metres at 2.44 g/t gold and 106 g/t silver, while a separate 253-metre-wide interval at 0.54 g/t gold at the adjacent Oculto East zone confirms the lateral scale of the system ahead of a planned Mineral Resource update. The combination of a high-grade core and a wide lower-grade halo is the structural profile needed to support bulk-mining economics and attracts the kind of resource scale that draws major producer interest.

headline: CENTURY LITHIUM CLEARS FEDERAL PERMITTING GATE — BLM Deems Angel Island Plan Complete, Environmental Review Opens
snippet: The US Bureau of Land Management ruled Century Lithium's (TSX-V: LCE) Angel Island Direct Lithium Extraction project in Nevada as administratively complete on November 9, formally opening the federal environmental review with a decision date targeted for February 4, 2028. The plan-completeness ruling triggers BLM's determination on whether an Environmental Assessment or a full Environmental Impact Statement is required — a key milestone on the permitting path for a project intended to supply US battery manufacturing.

headline: CODELCO ADMITS 42,100-TONNE OUTPUT OVERSTATEMENT — Nine Fired, Andina Halted by Tailings Spill, 2026 Guidance Cut
snippet: Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, confirmed it had overstated production by 42,100 tonnes across 2024 and 2025 — caused by mines recording material as finished output prematurely and creating duplicate records — estimating a $120–$140 million financial impact and cutting 2026 guidance to approximately 1.2 million tonnes; nine staff have been fired with audits ongoing. The disclosure landed simultaneously with a tailings spill that forced a halt to processing at the Andina operation while regulators demanded technical records within two business days, compounding investor concern about operational controls at the state miner that ranks first globally by output.

headline: BUNKER HILL SILVER CORP BORN — Silver47 Merger Closed Nov 6, 388M AgEq Oz Combined, $158M Market Cap on TSX
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining completed its merger with Silver47 Exploration on November 6, issuing 36.3 million new shares at a 0.1724x ratio to create a combined 388 million AgEq oz portfolio — 80 million oz Measured and Indicated plus 308 million oz Inferred — with a pro forma market cap of $158 million trading as the renamed Bunker Hill Silver Corp on the TSX. The combined entity holds an operating mine in Idaho's Silver Valley plus Silver47's development properties in Alaska, Nevada and New Mexico, positioning it as a 'Made in America' silver and critical minerals producer at a moment when silver sits on the US critical minerals list.

headline: RIO TINTO GREENLIGHTS $144M FOR RESOLUTION COPPER — Feasibility Engineering Funded on Path to 2030s Arizona Production
snippet: Rio Tinto approved a $144 million investment in the 55/45 Resolution Copper joint venture with BHP in Arizona — covering feasibility studies, final engineering for shaft material handling systems and new water treatment facilities — additional to the roughly $500 million in preliminary spending committed after the March 2026 land exchange. The funding does not represent a final construction decision but advances the work package required before one, with production projected in the mid-2030s and an estimated $1 billion annually in Arizona economic output.

headline: CITI CUTS LITHIUM FORECAST 40% TO $12,000/t — 2027 Glut Fear Deepens as Equities Already Down 33% From May Peak
snippet: Citi cut its near-term lithium carbonate price forecast by as much as 40% — from $20,000 to approximately $12,000 per tonne — citing slower battery demand growth and elevated trade uncertainty, a bearish call that deepens the pessimism already visible in lithium equities down 33.5% from their May 2026 peak. For ASX and TSX-V lithium developers weighing project timelines, the Citi cut compresses the near-term equity valuation floor while structural demand projections — 134 new mines needed by 2050, per recent SMM analysis — remain intact over the longer development cycle.

headline: GOLD OR COPPER — NEWMONT POSTS RECORD CASH FLOWS AS FREEPORT BETS ON GRASBERG RESTART
snippet: A Motley Fool November 8 analysis frames gold and copper mining as offering distinct risk-return profiles at current prices: Newmont generating record operational cash flows at sustained $4,000+ gold while trading well below its 52-week high, versus Freeport-McMoRan's higher leverage to the copper supercycle thesis dependent on a successful Grasberg restart. For retail investors deciding between the metals, the piece argues the two capture different macro scenarios — sticky inflation under the Warsh Fed (gold) versus the AI and EV copper demand wave that markets sharply repriced after the midterm results.

headline: BREAKING CHINA'S RARE EARTH GRIP — Pentagon's 2027 DFARS Deadline Makes Western Processing Non-Negotiable
snippet: A Daily Signal analysis argues that the Pentagon's DFARS procurement restriction on Chinese-sourced magnets — taking effect for defence equipment in fiscal 2027 and aligning with the January 10, 2027 expiry of China's export control pause — creates a hard, non-negotiable market for Western rare earth processing that cannot be met by the current approved project pipeline. The piece highlights Energy Fuels' White Mesa Mill in Utah as the most advanced Western processing facility, noting it leverages existing uranium infrastructure to produce rare earth carbonates and metals for DoD supply chain diversification.
